payload.instructions: Preserve all candidate IDs and distinctions. Broader parent themes organize evidence; they do not imply measurement equivalence.

themes.disagreements: contradictions, weak signals, and proxy distinctions
evidence_ids: at most 12 representative supplied modeling evidence IDs
themes.interpretation: common or complementary evidence
themes.name: theme

themes.disagreements: Radiation therapy (263) shows weaker univariable signals compared to platinum chemotherapy (267) and specific regimens (268).
themes.interpretation: Prior systemic oncology treatments show strong evidence as both confounders (predicting treatment) and prognostic factors (predicting outcome), with complementary signals for effect modification.
themes.name: Prior Oncology Treatments

themes.disagreements: The univariable signals are exceptionally strong for both treatment and outcome, potentially masking nuanced effect modification seen in causal forests.
themes.interpretation: Patient-reported symptoms (pain severity and exertional symptoms) are powerful predictors of both the treatment assigned and the final outcome, while also showing evidence for modifying the treatment effect.
themes.name: Symptomatic Burden

themes.disagreements: The extreme signals for both treatment and outcome are consistent across univariable and forest models, though penalized main effects are slightly more attenuated than univariable results.
themes.interpretation: Patient-reported outcome measures (PROs) reflecting functional status strongly predict both treatment assignment and outcome prognosis.
themes.name: Functional Quality of Life (PROs)

themes.disagreements: Evidence for treatment prediction is relatively consistent (predictive forests), but signals for treatment-heterogeneity (R-learners, Causal forests) vary significantly in strength and fold consistency.
themes.interpretation: Pulmonary imaging and diagnostic markers frequently predict treatment but show limited or inconsistent main outcome effects, suggesting roles as either instruments or effect modifiers.
themes.name: Pulmonary Diagnostics

themes.disagreements: The group includes a mixture of a clear confounder (PPI), an effect modifier (Psychiatric symptoms), and a candidate showing dual signals (Pupil reactivity).
themes.interpretation: General medical and neurological comorbidities provide heterogeneous evidence for confounding and treatment-heterogeneity.
themes.name: Medical and Neurological History

themes.disagreements: Treatment prediction is strong for radiation session count (281), while radiosurgery history (282) is primarily a strong prognostic factor.
themes.interpretation: Radiation-related history shows consistent evidence for treatment heterogeneity across different modalities.
themes.name: Radiation History

themes.disagreements: Signals for range of motion (283) and rash presence (284) are weak and inconsistent; rash/pruritus (285) shows a more robust prognostic and heterogeneity signal.
themes.interpretation: Cutaneous and sensory indicators vary in strength, with the combined rash/pruritus measure providing the most reliable signal.
themes.name: Cutaneous and Sensory Indicators

themes.disagreements: Respiratory rate (287) is a powerful predictor of both treatment and outcome, whereas renal function (286) primarily predicts treatment.
themes.interpretation: Systemic vital signs and organ function show high utility for treatment prediction, with respiratory rate acting as a probable confounder.
themes.name: Systemic Vitals and Renal Function

themes.disagreements: RET status (289) shows stronger treatment prediction, while DWI/ADC (288) and lymphadenopathy (290) lean more toward outcome prognosis and effect modification.
themes.interpretation: Radiological and molecular markers demonstrate moderate to strong evidence for effect modification.
themes.name: Radiological and Molecular Markers

themes.disagreements: Feature 291 shows strong treatment prediction but a weak outcome signal; feature 292 shows very low support across all roles.
themes.interpretation: Evidence identifies ROS1 mutation status as a strong treatment predictor and credible effect modifier, while rearrangement status remains weakly supportive across models.
themes.name: ROS1 Genetic Status

themes.disagreements: Relative signal strength varies: creatinine (299) and albumin (295) are dominant treatment predictors, while calcium (297) is a stronger outcome predictor.
themes.interpretation: Serum chemistry markers exhibit strong and consistent evidence for both confounding (predicting treatment and outcome) and effect modification.
themes.name: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP)

themes.disagreements: Feature 293 is entirely non-evaluable, whereas 294 shows a high support fraction for outcome prediction.
themes.interpretation: Scapular metastasis is a strong outcome predictor and a credible effect modifier; RSV infection status provided no evaluable evidence.
themes.name: Clinical and Pathological Status

themes.disagreements: smoking_abstinence_date is entirely unevaluable; smoking_status shows weaker signals than smoking_cessation_duration.
themes.interpretation: Features related to tobacco use exhibit strong evidence for treatment prediction, particularly for cessation duration.
themes.name: Smoking History

themes.disagreements: sulci_and_cisterns_appearance shows strong effect modification but lacks the strong outcome prognostic signal seen in subdural_hemorrhage.
themes.interpretation: Imaging features of the skull and brain show consistent importance for both outcome prognosis and treatment effect heterogeneity.
themes.name: Cranial Neuroimaging Findings

themes.disagreements: Signals are moderate (support fractions 0.5-0.6) and lack the high-confidence univariable p-values seen in imaging or smoking duration.
themes.interpretation: Biological sex and STK11 mutation status show mixed signals across treatment, outcome, and effect scales.
themes.name: Patient Demographics and Genetics

themes.disagreements: No support for role as a prognostic factor or treatment predictor.
themes.interpretation: Presence of skeletal compression fractures is strongly linked to treatment effect heterogeneity.
themes.name: Skeletal Manifestations

themes.disagreements: Low support fractions and high p-values suggest this candidate is likely non-contributory.
themes.interpretation: Serum sodium demonstrates weak and inconsistent evidence across all roles.
themes.name: Electrolyte Balance

themes.disagreements: Causal forest support for t_stage is stronger than R-learner support.
themes.interpretation: Features characterizing the surgical outcome and tumor extent show consistent evidence for effect modification across R-learner and causal forest models.
themes.name: Surgical and Pathological Status

themes.disagreements: Systolic blood pressure shows near-universal support, whereas tissue thickening relies on specific model families.
themes.interpretation: Measurements of systemic physiology and localized tissue characteristics are strong predictors of both treatment assignment and outcome prognosis.
themes.name: Clinical and Physiological Baseline

themes.disagreements: High consistency for tiotropium contradicts the weak or fragmented signals for targeted therapy, NGS, and TKI use.
themes.interpretation: Prior medication and testing exhibit varying levels of importance; tiotropium use is a strong predictor of treatment and outcome, while others are weak.
themes.name: Treatment and Diagnostic History

system:
You review pretreatment candidate measurements using modeling evidence
from one outer-training fold. First identify themes across candidates; then
reconcile their roles as confounder, effect_modifier, both, or neither.
All evidence is fallible. No individual family, p-value, or support frequency is
a hard selection gate. A credible complementary signal can justify retention
even when other methods shrink it away. Do not mistake correlated aliases or
proxies for multiple independent discoveries. Themes organize evidence; they
do not establish equivalence, merge measurements, or transfer a role to every
theme member. Preserve investigator-locked roles exactly.

Treatment prediction, outcome prognosis, and confounding are distinct. Discuss
whether a candidate could be a common cause rather than an instrument or only a
prognostic factor. Effect modification needs treatment-heterogeneity evidence;
outcome main-effect importance alone does not establish it. Univariable logistic
interactions are on the log-odds scale and unadjusted for other covariates.
Orthogonal linear models, candidate R-learners, and causal forests assess the
probability/outcome scale after elastic-net nuisance adjustment. Their targets
and biases differ. A model family is evidence, not an independent replication.

Use exposure and evaluability denominators. Missing or nonconverged fits are not
negative votes. Repeated samples and folds overlap; support fractions are not
causal probabilities or formal stability-selection error guarantees. Raw and BH
p-values do not correct the upstream adaptive discovery process. Permutation
importance can be diluted by correlated alternatives and does not prove a
causal role. Compare fold consistency, methods, subsets, and conflicting facts.
Definitions and theme names cannot establish a role without the supplied
empirical evidence. Never invent an oracle, data-generating process, or hidden
truth. Return the requested JSON and cite only supplied evidence IDs.
